messages.subject: Re: Stan’s Within-Chain Parallelization
messages.body_plain:
Hi David Munoz,

I've used within-chain parallelization of the latest Stan (with map_rect using cmdstanr) in my private projects. I ran my models to compute the log-likelihood for each participant with different CPU codes in a parallelized manner, and it was very helpful especially with datasets with large subjects in the multi-core server environment. However, it hasn't been applied to the codebase of hBayesDM yet.

Incorporating within-chain parallelization into hBayesDM seems to be a good idea, but I'm afraid there are several issues. For example, the current stan codes should be modified to use map_rect to calculate their likelihoods, and it would take time. Also, from some models in hBayesDM, users can extract model-based regressors. Those regressors may still require non-parallelized computations, which may not benefit from within-chain parallelization. Furthermore, within-chain parallelization may be applied across subjects, not across trials, because of dependencies in the data across trials from a subject. Due to this aspect, running hBayesDM with large-subject datasets can benefit from within-chain parallelization (as I did in my personal experiences), but it's unclear if it can also provide noticeable improvements even with usual cases in the subject number.

It would be great to incorporate within-chain parallelization into hBayesDM so that users who want to analyze large-subject datasets can benefit from its improvement. However, considering those issues I mentioned above, it seems to cost time to use it with hBayesDM yet.

Best regards,
Jaeyeong Yang

I'm wondering if anyone has tried modifying the ra_prospect script to run a combination of mixed gambles and loss only gambles, i.e. when the choice is between a certain small loss and a larger unlikely loss. I've modified the stan model and the scripts, but for some reason I keep getting "WARNING: empty program" and then that the Stan model doesn't contain samples. I'd appreciate help if anyone has any ideas.

Thanks!
Zoe

messages.subject: LOOIC of hierarchical model
messages.body_plain:
Dear hBayesDM user,

I am a MPhil student who is working on the Probabilistic Reversal Learning Task. Thanks for contributors there are various model available in hBayesDM.

In my experiment, each subject would do the PRL task seperated into four different blocks (with different stimuli), and each block contains 120 trials.

I wrote a simple model based on the Rescorla-Wagner (Delta) Model (prl_delta_multipleB) and some addition to the existing Stan files of the prl_rp and prl_fictitious_rp to fit the multiple block structure of my data.

So I have four different models for comparison:
1) prl_delta_multipleB
2) prl_fictitious_multipleB
3) prl_rp_multipleB
4) prl_fictitious_rp_multipleB

When comparing these model and select one that I will use to extract the trial-by-trial regressors for my model-based EEG analysis, I print out the LOOIC for each model. However, I have question regarding how the LOOIC is calculated in these hierarchical models. I assume printFit do the leave-one-trial-out cross-validation to compute the LOOIC.

Is it possible to do leave-one-block-out or leave-one-subject-out cross-validation instead of leave-one-trial-out? Alternatively, is there way I can use the loo package on the fitted hBayesDM object to achieve that?

Regards,
Ken
